etymology: Originally a tattooing needle making its mark — a distinguishing sign: a badge; in texts, the marked-off unit: a chapter.
mnemonic: The stamp pressed at the end of a section: this part is sealed — ショウ. Chapters and medals are the same thing: marks that say 'unit complete'.

etymology: Phono-semantic: tree (木) + 直 'straight' (phonetic ショク) — setting a sapling in straight: to plant.
mnemonic: Hold the sapling plumb-straight (直) while the soil goes in — うえる. 植物: everything that got planted and stayed.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 罙 'reach far in' (phonetic シン) — water you can reach into without touching bottom: deep.
mnemonic: Arm in to the shoulder and still no floor — ふかい. Deep water, deep night (深夜), deep thoughts: same missing bottom.

meaning: state humbly, sign of the monkey
etymology: Pictograph: forked lightning stretching down — the gods declaring themselves; hence to state (humbly, 申す), and the zodiac monkey by borrowing.
mnemonic: Lightning speaks first, you answer politely — もうす. 申します: introducing yourself under a sky that outranks you.

etymology: Phono-semantic: altar (示/ネ) + 申 'lightning' (phonetic シン) — the power addressed at the altar, announced in lightning: the gods.
mnemonic: Where lightning meets the altar — かみ. 神社 is the address; 神様 the resident.

etymology: Pictograph: a torso in profile with a full belly — originally a pregnant body: the living body, one's person.
mnemonic: A silhouette carrying life in its belly — み. 身体 is the body; 中身 the body of anything — what's carried inside.

etymology: Compound: a bundle (束) tapped by a hand (攵) until correct (正) — knocked into order: to arrange, adjust.
mnemonic: Tap the stack square on the desk until every edge is 正 — ととのえる. 整理: the satisfying thunk of order.

etymology: Compound ideograph: layers (廿) piled over days (日) — days heaped on days: long ago, antiquity.
mnemonic: Day pressed on day like sediment — むかし. Every folktale drills into the same stratum: 昔々, once upon a time.

etymology: Compound ideograph: flawless jade (王) kept under cover (𠆢) — intact, untouched: whole, complete.
mnemonic: The gem still in its case, not a scratch — ゼン. 全部, 全然, 安全: wholeness, in stock, on sale, and kept safe.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 相 'facing, mutual' (phonetic ソウ) + heart (心) — the heart facing an image of what isn't there: to imagine, conceive.
mnemonic: The heart holds a picture up and studies it — ソウ. 思想 is a gallery of them; 可哀想 is the picture that hurts to look at.

etymology: Compound ideograph: an eye (目) examining a tree (木) — observer and observed facing each other: mutual, reciprocal; an aspect; a minister who 'oversees'.
mnemonic: You look at the tree; on some level the tree looks back — あい. 相手: the one on the other end of your gaze.

etymology: Compound ideograph: nose (自) over heart (心) — the current running between nose and heart: breath; a son (one's own breath continued).
mnemonic: Air rides from the nose down to the heart and back — いき. 休息 is when you finally hear it; 息子 is your breath walking around outside you.

etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 束 'tied bundle' (phonetic ソク) — strapped tight and speeding: fast.
mnemonic: Cinch the pack down and nothing rattles: pure speed — はやい. The 高速 is where tight bundles overtake loose ones.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 也 (phonetic タ) — some person over there, not this one: other.
mnemonic: A figure trailing off in another direction — ほか. その他: everyone and everything the sentence didn't name.

etymology: Phono-semantic: hand (扌) + 丁 'nail' (phonetic ダ/チョウ) — the hand coming down on the nail: to strike.
mnemonic: Hammer-hand meets nail head — うつ. Baseball took it (打つ, batting), and so did your keyboard: 打ち込む.

etymology: Simplified from 對: a hand (寸) answering a rack of bells — to respond in kind, face to face: versus, vis-à-vis.
mnemonic: Two players squared up across the table — タイ. 3対2, 反対, 対する: everything that stands facing something else.

etymology: Phono-semantic: bamboo (⺮) + 弟 'birth-order' (phonetic ダイ) — bamboo slips filed in sequence: number so-and-so.
mnemonic: The bamboo tags on a string, each with its rank — ダイ. 第一 hangs first; everything else queues behind it.

etymology: Compound: fire (火) burning under the mountain's cliff (山+厂) — the kiln in the hillside: charcoal, coal.
mnemonic: Fire sealed in the hill until wood turns black and light — すみ. The yakitori grill still runs on this kanji.

etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 炎 'blaze' (phonetic ダン) — talk by the fire, or talk that catches like one: discussion.
mnemonic: Words traded across a campfire, sparks included — ダン. 相談 is bringing your problem to that fire.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 主 'master' (phonetic チュウ) — the master timber the whole house hangs on: the pillar.
mnemonic: One post holds the roof the way the master holds the household — はしら. Remove it and everything above remembers why it mattered.

etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 周 'all the way around' (phonetic チョウ) — checking a thing from every side: to tune, adjust, investigate.
mnemonic: Walk your questions all the way around it (周) until it sounds right — しらべる. 調べる investigates; 調子 is the tuning you're in today.

etymology: Compound: movement (辶) + 𠂤 'massed troops' — marching after a retreating column: to pursue, chase.
mnemonic: Their dust cloud is still visible — go! — おう. 追いかける: the whole kanji at a sprint.

etymology: Compound ideograph: things set correct (正) under the roof (宀) — settled in place: fixed, determined.
mnemonic: Everything in the house squared and bolted — さだめる, テイ. 予定, 定食: the schedule and the set meal — life pre-decided.

etymology: Phono-semantic: building (广) + 廷 'royal court' (phonetic テイ) — the open ground within the walls: courtyard, garden.
mnemonic: The palace court shrunk to fit behind your house — にわ. Every 庭 keeps a little ceremony in its gravel.

etymology: Simplified from 鐵: metal (金) + a phonetic now written 失 — the workhorse metal: iron.
mnemonic: The metal that loses (失) its shine and keeps its strength — てつ. 地下鉄: iron veins under the city.

etymology: Compound ideograph: feet set apart (癶) climbing with the offering vessel (豆) — mounting the altar steps: to ascend.
mnemonic: Step by step up the shrine stairs, bowl held level — のぼる. 登山 is the same climb with a bigger altar.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a bird (鳥, tail clipped) on a mountain (山) rising from the sea — where seabirds rest: an island.
mnemonic: A peak just big enough for the gulls to land — しま. Japan: one country, 14,000 of these kanji.

etymology: Compound ideograph: hand (扌) + 殳 'lance' — the hand hurling the weapon: to throw.
mnemonic: Wind-up, release: spear away — なげる. The pitcher (投手) does it for a living, mercifully with a ball.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 昜 'sun blazing up' (phonetic トウ) — water with the sun in it: hot water.
mnemonic: Water heated until it glows like sunrise — ゆ. The ♨ sign and the sentō curtain both spell this one kanji.

etymology: Compound: bamboo slips (⺮) sorted at the office (寺) — graded into equal ranks: equal; 'and the rest of the same grade': etc.
mnemonic: Slips of the same length in the same box — ひとしい. 一等 is the top box; 等々 waves at all the boxes you didn't list.

etymology: Grim origin: a tattooed (辛-marked) servant child; the meaning softened over centuries to simply 'child'.
mnemonic: The kanji grew up gentler than it was born: now it just means kids — わらべ, ドウ. 児童 in school, 童話 at bedtime.

etymology: Compound ideograph: field rows worked with the shell-hoe (辰 — a clamshell blade) — dawn labor on the land: agriculture.
mnemonic: A clamshell lashed to a stick, scraping rows before sunrise — ノウ. 農家: the people who fed everyone with a seashell.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 皮 'skin' (phonetic ハ) — the sea's moving skin: waves.
mnemonic: The ocean flexing its hide — なみ. Radio waves, heat waves, 津波: everything that travels as rolling skin.

etymology: Compound ideograph: an attendant (己) kneeling at the wine jar (酉), portioning it out — to distribute, allot; the allotted partner: spouse.
mnemonic: Cup by cup around the table, no one skipped — くばる. 心配 is your heart doing rounds it wasn't asked to do.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 咅 (phonetic バイ) — originally to split away, and a thing split makes two: double, -fold.
mnemonic: Cut the mochi in half: now you have two — バイ. 二倍, 三倍: multiplication by cheerful cutting.

etymology: Phono-semantic: bamboo (⺮) + 相 (phonetic ソウ→はこ) — the woven bamboo chest: a box.
mnemonic: Bamboo strips facing each other (相) until they close into walls — はこ. 箱根: the box canyon with hot springs in it.

etymology: A kokuji — invented in Japan: fire (火) + field (田) — land cleared by burning for dry crops (no paddy water): a farm field.
mnemonic: Burn the brush, plant the slope: the dry field — はたけ. Japan built this kanji itself, ash and all.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (又) pressed against the cliff (厂), pushing back — to turn over, oppose: anti-.
mnemonic: Palm flat on the rock face, shoving the other way — ハン. 反対 is the shove made official.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 反 (phonetic ハン) — wood flipped and planed flat: a board.
mnemonic: Turn the log, shave; turn, shave — until it's a plank — いた. The 黒板 and the 掲示板 are its indoor careers.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 非 'pulled apart in two directions' (phonetic ヒ) + heart (心) — a heart split open: sorrow.
mnemonic: Two wings tearing away from each other with the heart between — かなしい. Grief is the heart's wishbone moment.

components: hide being stripped by a hand
etymology: Pictograph: a hand stripping the hide from a carcass — skin, pelt, bark, peel.
mnemonic: The hand at the bottom is mid-peel — かわ. Banana skin, tree bark, dumpling wrapper: all 皮 to Japanese.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a big (大) sheep (羊) — the fattest, finest animal brought for offering: fine, beautiful.
mnemonic: The prize sheep, groomed and gleaming, led up the aisle — うつくしい. Beauty began as the best thing you could give.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 自 (the original nose pictograph) + 畀 (phonetic ビ) — added when 自 drifted off to mean 'oneself': the nose proper.
mnemonic: The old nose (自) needed scaffolding once 'self' stole it: behold the full apparatus — はな. Biggest kanji on the face.

etymology: Compound ideograph: bamboo (⺮) + 聿 'hand gripping a brush' — the bamboo-handled writing brush.
mnemonic: Bamboo shaft, wolf-hair tip, hand steady — ふで. The 鉛筆 is its graphite grandchild.

etymology: Compound: water (水) with a single freezing drop added — water gone solid: ice.
mnemonic: Water with one extra chip in it: frozen — こおり. The shaved-ice flags of summer fly this kanji, かき氷.
